work_packages.title: Establish operating kit and verified baseline
work_packages.steps: Read 00, the canonical register, findings and local AGENTS; record source SHA, both CLI versions and dirty worktree. Install only repo-local guide/skill files after implementation authorization. Run the harness evaluation matrix in disposable fixtures. Assign disjoint work areas.
work_packages.acceptance: OpenCode v2 (the only harness, CHG-006) discovers the canonical workflows, respects deny rules, loads nested guidance and resumes a fresh handoff. Preserve existing unrelated edits. No application code is changed by this package.
work_packages.handoff: Record exact commit, files, evidence, remaining gate and next unblocked task in the task record.
work_packages.acceptance_original: Both actual harnesses discover the canonical workflows, respect deny rules, load nested guidance and resume a fresh handoff. Preserve existing unrelated edits. No application code is changed by this package.

work_packages.title: Separate credentials and restrict public sharing
work_packages.steps: Remove FRM-token flow into ngrok auth configuration/argv. Separate the FRM credential from provider account credentials in types, UI and main-process configuration. Refuse automatic public sharing until selected FRM authentication and target are verified; document complete API exposure. Implement the narrow main-owned profile and single-use share-permit contracts in02 section10; main performs the FRM auth probe and never trusts a renderer success boolean.
work_packages.acceptance: Dummy FRM token cannot reach ngrok options, argv, logs or provider configuration. Empty/failed FRM authentication blocks public sharing. Normal private FRM connections still work.
work_packages.handoff: Record exact commit, files, evidence, remaining gate and next unblocked task in the task record.

work_packages.title: Make tunnel lifecycle serialized and observable
work_packages.steps: Replace multiple global/process paths with one tunnel adapter and explicit state machine. Serialize start/stop, retain ownership until child exit, abort starts on Stop, bound output, and kill owned process trees on failure and shutdown.
work_packages.acceptance: Timeout, exit, cancellation, concurrent starts and stop-during-start cannot leave an untracked tunnel. UI never reports stopped while closure is unconfirmed. Mocks plus local real-process tests pass. Origin/token change, Forget, disconnect, reload and renderer loss invoke the same stop path. Abrupt-main-death recovery preserves closure_unknown through a nonsecret ownership marker.
work_packages.handoff: Record exact commit, files, evidence, remaining gate and next unblocked task in the task record.

work_packages.title: Constrain Electron IPC and navigation
work_packages.steps: Validate WebContents/main-frame sender and expected local app URL on every IPC channel. Validate typed input in main, bind tunnel targets to the approved FRM profile, deny unexpected navigation/windows and permissions. Keep Node integration disabled and context isolation enabled.
work_packages.acceptance: Untrusted frame/sender, malformed ports/hosts and mismatched targets are rejected before any side effect. Expected UI operations pass. Renderer sandbox and security defaults remain enabled.
work_packages.handoff: Record exact commit, files, evidence, remaining gate and next unblocked task in the task record.

work_packages.title: Upgrade supported desktop runtime and packaging
work_packages.steps: Update Electron to the selected supported candidate, modernize builder and its transitive graph, and keep React/Next separate from desktop runtime reachability. Inventory packaged modules and exact Chromium/Node/native binaries. Validate Windows and Linux locally.
work_packages.acceptance: Exact resolved Electron version is supported on release day; packaged runtime versions/SBOM match source/build evidence. No untriaged high/critical runtime finding. Both desktop packaging baselines launch and exercise connection/IPC tests; integrated CLI/tunnel validation is owned by WP-06/WP-11 at G-04.
work_packages.handoff: Record exact commit, files, evidence, remaining gate and next unblocked task in the task record.
work_packages.blocker: Sandboxed Electron GUI launch blocked (chrome-sandbox not root-owned mode 4755); Windows execution not run on Linux host.

work_packages.title: Patch frontend and development dependency families

work_packages.acceptance: Both full lockfile scans rerun successfully, exact fixed ranges are satisfied, and static build/test behavior is validated. Exceptions record reachability evidence, owner and expiry, not only a scanner suppression.

work_packages.title: Remove legacy ngrok wrapper and verify native artifact
work_packages.steps: Replace legacy npm ngrok with one narrow direct CLI adapter, reusing existing child-process concepts. Pin the vendor CLI version and digest through a trusted acquisition path; use machine-readable status/config, never PATH fallback or a mutable stable download. Keep provider credentials outside renderer/argv.
work_packages.acceptance: No old wrapper or its advisory paths remain in either lockfile or packages. Build manifest proves bundled CLI version, source and digest. Wrong-platform/tampered artifact fails closed. No lifecycle scripts download an unrecorded native binary.
work_packages.handoff: Record exact commit, files, evidence, remaining gate and next unblocked task in the task record.
work_packages.blocker: No trusted ngrok CLI artifact/digest supplied; sharing fails closed. Real provider start cannot be tested.

work_packages.title: Preserve transport intent and bind credentials to origin
work_packages.steps: Centralize URL parsing and validation. Preserve explicit scheme/port, support IPv6, reject userinfo/query/fragment/path ambiguity, correctly classify private addresses, and require explicit acknowledgement for plaintext LAN credentials. Reject authenticated redirects and clear secret on origin change.
work_packages.acceptance: HTTPS never becomes HTTP; ports survive normalization. Cross-origin or downgraded redirects never receive the token. Changing origin requires a newly entered credential. Loopback and allowed LAN use remain possible.
work_packages.handoff: Record exact commit, files, evidence, remaining gate and next unblocked task in the task record.

work_packages.title: Remove durable plaintext tokens and migrate settings
work_packages.steps: Persist only schema-validated nonsecret preferences. Keep FRM token in memory for this security release; remove legacy password fields and add Forget connection. Reject malformed local settings safely. Defer protected persistent secret storage to a separate change.
work_packages.acceptance: Reload, restart, Forget and origin change remove the in-memory token. Existing localStorage token is deleted during migration. New app-generated exports, logs, fixtures, crash samples and backups contain no token; migration removes active legacy storage but cannot erase historical copies outside app control.
work_packages.handoff: Record exact commit, files, evidence, remaining gate and next unblocked task in the task record.

work_packages.title: Bound API work and ignore stale responses
work_packages.steps: Add shared cancellation/timeout, response byte and shape limits, in-flight limits, connection generation guards, backoff and bounded polling history. Preserve escaped text rendering; validate numeric/array fields before expensive map/recipe operations.
work_packages.acceptance: Oversized or malformed responses and never-ending requests fail with a recoverable error. An old response cannot populate a new connection. Polling cannot multiply after remounts or failures. Boundary fixtures pass under controlled clocks.
work_packages.handoff: Record exact commit, files, evidence, remaining gate and next unblocked task in the task record.

work_packages.title: Add defensive document policy and truthful security UX
work_packages.steps: Introduce a production CSP compatible with static Next hydration, restrictive executable sources and documented connection policy. Label secret purposes; expose sharing/error/unknown states and keyboard-accessible stop/recovery actions. Restrict desktop navigation/permissions.
work_packages.acceptance: Production app has a tested CSP without unsafe-eval or unrestricted script sources; no required panel breaks. Keyboard users can connect/cancel/stop/recover, and status announces the actual state. No claim that broad HTTP(S) connect-src alone prevents exfiltration.

decisions.title: Retain static Next/React plus Electron
decisions.rationale: Avoid a framework/language rewrite unrelated to confirmed defects. Keep current panel boundaries and use narrow shared functions.
decisions.reconsider_when: Reconsider only if supported runtime/patch upgrades cannot satisfy a demonstrated requirement.

decisions.title: Use exact locked versions and applicability evidence
decisions.rationale: CVE/GHSA matches establish affected installed versions; runtime reachability is a separate record. Keep native-runtime candidates separate.
decisions.reconsider_when: Recheck at every lockfile change and within 24 hours of release.

decisions.title: Use session-only FRM tokens in the security release
decisions.rationale: Removing durable plaintext storage is the smallest reliable fix. Preserve nonsecret preferences and migrate old password fields away.
decisions.reconsider_when: Protected opt-in persistence may be a later separately reviewed feature; never silently fall back to plaintext.

decisions.title: Use one pinned direct ngrok CLI adapter
decisions.rationale: Reuse existing child-process design while removing vulnerable wrapper, multiple fallback paths and mutable native downloads. Provider credentials remain main-process/local-provider configuration.
decisions.reconsider_when: Reconsider official SDK only with proven platform packaging benefit and a new dependency/threat review.

decisions.title: Preserve LAN operation with explicit plaintext acknowledgement
decisions.rationale: FRM commonly runs on a local HTTP listener. Preserve that capability while honoring explicit HTTPS and making credential risk visible.
decisions.reconsider_when: Public-IP HTTP is rejected; owner can use TLS/VPN for remote/LAN traffic.
decisions.clarification: Plain HTTP is allowed for localhost/loopback and parsed RFC1918 IPv4 or IPv6 ULA literals with the stated acknowledgement. Plain HTTP DNS names and public literals are rejected; use a private literal or HTTPS. This conservative browser-portable policy avoids unverifiable DNS-locality claims.

decisions.title: Keep local validation as the delivery gate
decisions.rationale: Do not add GitHub Actions. Existing release/code-analysis workflows are assessed and require owner decision before future edits.
decisions.reconsider_when: Only a later explicit request authorizes new Actions.

decisions.title: One canonical JSON register; workbook is a proposed-edit view
decisions.rationale: Avoid competing status/approval truth. Stable IDs allow human workbook proposals to be reviewed and merged.
decisions.reconsider_when: Integrate edited rows by ID and baseline revision; reject stale/unknown/conflicting IDs.

decisions.title: Share canonical skill bodies between harnesses
decisions.rationale: Use proposed .agents/skills definitions supported by both official documents; keep role/permission syntax in small tool-specific adapters.
decisions.reconsider_when: No portability claim until both installed tool versions pass the local evaluation matrix.

decisions.title: Security interaction specifications replace visual mockups
decisions.rationale: This is a review/remediation plan for an existing UI. State/label/accessibility contracts are sufficient; new branding/screens are not in scope.
decisions.reconsider_when: Generate mockups only for a later explicitly approved UI redesign.

decisions.title: Current candidate families require actual resolution and regression gates
decisions.rationale: Use sourced candidate versions, never claim that a package proposal or an install-free scan is a tested application upgrade.
decisions.reconsider_when: Re-resolve if work starts after the report date, a patch is superseded, or compatibility gates fail.

decisions.title: No new backend, account system or operational platform
decisions.rationale: Authentication is an FRM/provider concern. This desktop/static client needs target/secret lifecycle controls and trustworthy builds, not SaaS infrastructure.
decisions.reconsider_when: Revisit only for an explicitly authorized multi-user hosted product.

decisions.title: Urgent containment is separate from general hardening
decisions.rationale: Contain automatic public sharing during P1 repairs. Restore it only after G-01/G-02/applicable G-03 and integrated G-04 evidence passes. Preserve private dashboard functionality.
decisions.reconsider_when: Recheck all sharing gates before restoration.

findings.title: FRM authentication token is sent to ngrok as its account credential
findings.status: Confirmed data-flow defect; dummy-token mock reproduced
findings.description: ConnectionBar passes config.password, labeled as the FRM Auth Token from WebServer.cfg, to tunnelStart. Preload forwards it unchanged. Main names the same argument authtoken and supplies it to ngrok.connect or the CLI --authtoken argument. The locked ngrok package also inserts this value into its agent argv. These are independent credentials for different services.
conditions: Electron Share is used with a nonempty FRM auth token.
At least one ngrok execution path is available.
findings.impact: The FRM secret reaches an unrelated subprocess and its process arguments; it is treated as a credential for the ngrok service and may cause sharing to fail or expose the secret to observers of command lines/agent diagnostics. Whether a malformed token is transmitted to ngrok or rejected locally was not tested. No claim that this call persists the token to ngrok's config: the exact locked connect implementation does not call setAuthtoken.
findings.severity_rationale: A concrete credential-boundary violation requiring the normal Share action. Scope is the FRM credential and sharing availability; no proven remote compromise or arbitrary command execution.
remediation_contract: Remove FRM credentials and arbitrary host/port from tunnelStart. The selected contract is tunnelStart({permitId}) after a separate main-owned FRM authentication probe; see02 section10. ngrok uses only its separately configured provider credential.
If in-app ngrok credential management is retained later, give it a distinct typed field and main-process/OS-backed storage; never reuse config.password or renderer localStorage for it.
Redact secrets in raw provider errors and logs. Keep FRM credentials limited to requests to the authorized FRM origin.
Update electron.d.ts and all setup docs to distinguish FRM API tokens from ngrok account tokens.
acceptance_tests: With distinct FRM_DUMMY and NGROK_DUMMY sentinels, assert FRM_DUMMY never appears in ngrok options, subprocess argv, provider errors, logs or ngrok configuration.
Verify Share works with a configured ngrok account when the FRM server requires authentication, and a missing ngrok credential produces a provider-specific error without changing the FRM token.
Exercise both the packaged binary and supported development execution path using dummy credentials and mocks first; any live integration test requires an isolated test account/service.
findings.confirmation: Confirmed data-flow defect; dummy-token mock reproduced

findings.title: Tunnel failures and start/stop races can leave public exposure outside application control
findings.confidence: High for control-flow defects; conditional public impact
findings.status: Confirmed with isolated timeout and late-completion mocks
findings.description: On CLI timeout or other caught start error, main clears ngrokProcess without first killing and awaiting the child. Subsequent Stop and window-close inspect only the cleared handle. Separately, a pending npm connect can finish after Stop has returned and reestablish ngrokUrl because start/stop have no serialization or cancellation generation. CLI success detection only recognizes human Forwarding lines despite requesting piped --log=stdout, for which ngrok documents structured/non-TTY log formats; valid structured success logs can therefore lead into the timeout path.
conditions: For the forgotten-child case, CLI fallback starts a real agent but the app does not recognize its URL before timeout; public impact requires the agent to have established a tunnel.
For the race case, Stop/shutdown or another operation overlaps a pending start. The current UI disables repeated start clicks while loading, but main-process IPC has no concurrency guard.
findings.impact: The application can report sharing failed/inactive or stopped while a tunnel remains live, or report a late active tunnel after Stop succeeded. An unauthenticated or weakly protected upstream service would remain internet reachable unexpectedly. Even an authenticated FRM service loses the intended exposure lifecycle. Severity can increase with the sensitivity/authentication of the selected upstream; no real tunnel or compromise was demonstrated.
findings.severity_rationale: Concrete loss of network-exposure control, but exploitation/data impact depends on an actual successful public tunnel and upstream authorization. Rated Medium for this game-dashboard scope rather than assuming full host compromise.
remediation_contract: Introduce one main-process tunnel owner with explicit idle/starting/active/stopping/error state, serialized operations and a generation/cancellation token.

Hold child handles locally during start. Every timeout, cancellation, parse failure, spawn error and shutdown must terminate the owned child, await exit, and verify cleanup before dropping ownership. Escalate kill only for that owned child if graceful termination fails.
Ignore and immediately clean up late results from cancelled starts. Make Stop idempotent and make its result reflect confirmed closure, not cleared variables.
Use a supported structured readiness mechanism: a parsed JSON log contract or the owned agent's loopback management API. Do not infer readiness solely from terminal UI text.
Bound/redact log buffers and remove listeners/timers on completion. Handle child error/exit directly; remove the global uncaughtException swallowing workaround.
Drive UI state from the owner, propagate start/stop errors, and await shutdown cleanup rather than fire-and-forget promises.
acceptance_tests: Fake a running CLI that never yields a recognized URL: timeout must call terminate and await exit; status cannot become inactive while the owned child is alive.
Provide representative structured success logs with split chunks; readiness is detected once and buffers remain bounded.
Race start/start, start/stop, timeout/start and shutdown/start; after Stop/shutdown returns, no earlier generation can become active and every child has one accountable owner.
Exercise spawn errors, zero/nonzero exit before readiness, exit after readiness, delayed npm connect, cleanup failures and platform-specific process termination with fake children.
In an isolated integration environment, prove the public endpoint is unreachable after stop/failure and verify that unrelated ngrok processes are unaffected.
findings.confirmation: Confirmed with isolated timeout and late-completion mocks

findings.title: Tunnel IPC trusts every sender and accepts unvalidated arbitrary targets
findings.confidence: High for missing guards; conditional exploitability
findings.status: Confirmed missing controls; no independent renderer compromise found
findings.description: The preload exposes tunnel start/stop/status to its page. Main ignores the event for start and does not inspect events for stop/status; host and port are interpolated without type, scheme, port-range or target-authorization validation. BrowserWindow has no navigation/window-open restrictions, so navigation to untrusted content is not explicitly prevented. A renderer that gains access to this bridge can request a public tunnel to an HTTP-reachable local/LAN service, stop the user's tunnel or read its URL.
conditions: Attacker must first gain JavaScript execution in a bridge-enabled renderer or cause bridge-enabled untrusted content to load, or have equivalent local execution/IPC access.
A usable ngrok account/agent is required for successful exposure.

No XSS or remote navigation entry point was demonstrated in the inspected renderer; its external text is predominantly React-escaped. A normal web page outside this Electron window cannot simply invoke these handlers.
findings.impact: Missing trust-boundary checks amplify a future renderer compromise into native public-tunnel control and potential exposure of unrelated local/LAN HTTP services. This is not evidence of generic command execution: the app's ngrok CLI call uses an argument array with no shell, and nodeIntegration is explicitly disabled.
findings.severity_rationale: A sensitive native capability lacks both caller and target authorization, but a prerequisite renderer compromise/navigation path is unresolved. Medium, not an unauthenticated standalone RCE claim.
remediation_contract: Validate every IPC sender: the expected live mainWindow.webContents, its top-level frame and a precisely authorized application origin/document; reject missing/destroyed frames, subframes, child windows and all unrelated origins. Avoid prefix matching and do not accept all file: URLs merely because their origin is null.
Prefer a dedicated secure application protocol with a fixed origin and constrained resource root. Until migrated, strictly identify the exact packaged document and its expected top-level frame.

Deny unintended navigation and new windows; add deny-by-default permission request/check handlers. Production packaged builds must not switch to localhost content merely because NODE_ENV or --dev is set.

Use a validated main-process FRM connection profile for sharing instead of a general arbitrary host/port tunnel primitive. Preserve legitimate local/LAN FRM support while parsing a hostname/IP, numeric port 1–65535, approved scheme and a user-selected target; reject file:, credential-bearing URLs, path/query/fragment injection, option-like inputs and malformed IPv6.
Keep nodeIntegration false and contextIsolation true. Explicit sandbox/webSecurity true can document intent, but their absence as explicit keys is not itself a defect on Electron 33.
acceptance_tests: Send mocked IPC from an unrelated webContents, child frame, missing senderFrame, https://untrusted.invalid, about:blank and arbitrary file URL: all handlers reject before calling ngrok or returning a URL.
Allow only the real main-frame application origin/document; packaged mode ignores developer environment switches.
External navigation/new-window attempts and unneeded permission requests are denied while all 12 dashboard tabs still work.

Reject non-string/oversized hosts, out-of-range ports, unsupported schemes, credentials, fragments, leading options and unrelated profile IDs; accept and correctly canonicalize supported localhost/LAN/IPv6 FRM profiles.
Ensure the hardened IPC does not expose raw ipcRenderer, generic process launch or arbitrary filesystem methods.
findings.diagnostic: electron_mock_results.json case 1; fake sender only, not a live attack
findings.confirmation: Confirmed missing controls; no independent renderer compromise found

findings.title: Packaged ngrok native binary is a mutable postinstall download outside lockfile integrity
findings.status: Confirmed build supply-chain control gap; no malicious binary observed
findings.description: package-lock pins the npm ngrok wrapper, but that wrapper's postinstall downloads ngrok-v3-stable from a mutable CDN URL and extracts it without a pinned cryptographic digest/signature check. package.json copies node_modules/ngrok/bin into the application. Runtime ensureNgrokNpmBinary checks executable magic/permission, which detects corrupt downloads but does not authenticate a native program. The fallback also resolves ngrok from PATH, outside the packaged binary's identity.
conditions: Dependencies are installed with lifecycle scripts enabled, as in release.yml npm ci.
The resulting native binary is packaged and later used for Share.

Compromise requires replacement of a trusted distribution/cache/build input or executable resolution; no such compromise was observed. HTTPS is used for the default download and was not found disabled.
findings.impact: Identical repository/lockfile inputs need not produce the same native binary, and reviewers cannot determine its version/content from the lockfile. A malicious substituted native binary would execute with the desktop user's privileges. This is a supply-chain gap, not proof that the current binary is malicious.
findings.severity_rationale: Native executable content lacks immutable identity, but adversarial exploitation requires compromise/tampering of an upstream or local build source. Medium hardening priority, with high potential impact if that prerequisite occurs.
remediation_contract: Choose a supported tunneling implementation after resolving the ngrok package advisory; do not downgrade blindly to another affected wrapper.

If shipping a native agent, pin its version and platform/architecture-specific trusted digest or signed manifest in reviewed build inputs, verify before packaging, and record the packaged binary's version/hash in an SBOM/release manifest.
Avoid implicit lifecycle-script downloads for release builds. Fetch verified native assets in an explicit auditable build step.

Do not silently replace a rejected/missing packaged binary with an arbitrary PATH result. Either fail closed or use an explicit separately selected, verified executable path with clear support semantics.
Keep magic/architecture checks as corruption diagnostics, not as the authenticity check.
acceptance_tests: Two clean builds use the same recorded native agent digest; changing upstream stable content cannot silently change the shipped executable.
A tampered binary retaining valid ELF/PE/Mach-O magic fails verification and is never executed or packaged.
A missing or mismatched packaged binary produces a clear error without executing an unexpected PATH binary.
Every supported Windows/Linux package contains an agent matching its manifest's version, platform, architecture and digest.
findings.confirmation: Confirmed build supply-chain control gap; no malicious binary observed

findings.title: Release dependency builds receive repository-write credentials and mutable actions
findings.confidence: High for configuration; upstream-compromise scenario conditional
findings.status: Confirmed workflow least-privilege and immutability gaps
findings.description: release.yml grants contents: write at workflow scope. Build jobs checkout with default credential persistence, run npm ci lifecycle scripts and tests, and explicitly expose GH_TOKEN during the build even though --publish never is set. Actions are referenced by movable v4/v2 tags. Therefore third-party install/build code and mutable action updates run in a job that can write repository content, although only the final release job needs that privilege.
conditions: The upstream release workflow is enabled and triggered by an authorized push to main.
An action, package lifecycle script or build dependency is compromised, or malicious code has already entered a trusted build input.
No evidence of a compromised action/package, stolen token, or bypass of repository protection was found. Release does not use pull_request_target.
findings.impact: A build-chain compromise may gain repository/tag/release write capability in addition to altering its immediate artifact. Mutable action tags can change executed workflow code without a diff in this repository.
findings.severity_rationale: Avoidable privilege amplification and mutable build dependencies, but not a direct untrusted-PR execution finding. Repository-level protection settings and external organizational controls were not inspected.
remediation_contract: If retaining this upstream GitHub Actions release mechanism, default workflow permissions to contents: read and grant contents: write only to the final isolated publish job.

Set persist-credentials: false for checkouts and remove GH_TOKEN from dependency installation, tests and build steps; no publishing credential should be available during arbitrary dependency script execution.
Pin actions to reviewed immutable commits, or adopt GitHub's supported workflow dependency lockfile where available, including transitive action dependencies.
The publish job should consume only artifacts/digests from the same verified workflow commit, verify manifests, and receive credentials only at publication time.

If the chosen project policy is local testing/releases without GitHub Actions, preserve these same build/publish credential separation and immutable-input requirements in the local process instead. Do not enable Actions as part of this planning review.
acceptance_tests: Static workflow validation proves all non-publish jobs have read-only or no repository token and no inherited contents: write.
A benign isolated build fixture cannot obtain write-capable credentials from environment or persisted git config; no real token is printed or exfiltrated.
Every action is locked to reviewed immutable code and dependency updates require a reviewable diff.
Release publication verifies commit identity and artifact hashes; normal build failures cannot publish and package scripts never run in the credentialed publisher.
findings.confirmation: Confirmed workflow least-privilege and immutability gaps

findings.title: Endpoint normalization silently downgrades explicitly requested HTTPS and misclassifies hosts
findings.summary: buildUrl discards an explicitly supplied http/https scheme and chooses HTTP for any host beginning 192.168., 10., or 172. It does not parse an IP address or respect an HTTPS user's choice. X-FRM-Authorization is then attached to the resulting URL. Explicit custom ports on DNS/IPv6 hosts are also silently discarded.
findings.preconditions: A user connects with an FRM token to an HTTP-reachable server, with network observation/modification possible. The downgrade is directly relevant to Electron/local HTTP app use. A browser serving the dashboard over HTTPS may block mixed-content requests instead; that is not an application-level guarantee.
findings.impact: Possible disclosure of the FRM token and monitored/game-chat data to an on-path party, and unintended connections or failure after custom ports are lost. No actual real-token disclosure was attempted.

evidence.claim: Scheme stripping, prefix-based classification, port loss, header attachment
The chat POST repeats the same behavior
Current tests encode some URL normalization behavior and omit downgrade/host-spoof cases

findings.remediation: Use one URL parser/canonicalizer shared by the connection UI and all transports. Preserve explicit HTTPS and effective ports. Reject userinfo, unexpected paths, query/fragment, unsupported schemes and invalid ports. Keep deliberate loopback/LAN HTTP compatibility but expose an explicit insecure-transport acknowledgement for non-loopback HTTP with a token. Private address classification never makes plaintext safe. Never downgrade after a certificate error.
acceptance_tests: Explicit https://192.168.1.50 stays HTTPS; no HTTP request occurs.
172.16.0.0/12 versus 172.1.2.3 and DNS names beginning 10./172./192.168. are distinguished correctly if address classification is needed.
Explicit :8443 survives normalization for DNS and IPv6; conflicting Host/Port entries produce a visible deterministic result.
Only HTTP(S) endpoints without credentials/query/fragment/path confusion can reach fetch; a real intended LAN HTTP configuration still works after acknowledgement.

findings.title: Credentialed fetches allow redirects to carry the custom FRM token to another origin
findings.summary: Both the shared client and API Explorer send X-FRM-Authorization with the default redirect policy. WHATWG Fetch follows redirects by default and removes the standard Authorization header when origins change, not arbitrary custom credential headers. The application does not enforce an origin boundary before redirects.
findings.preconditions: The configured server or an intervening HTTP/tunnel/reverse-proxy response redirects to another origin, and the browser's CORS/preflight rules permit that chain and target. A malicious target can permit the custom header; a fully compromised source server already sees the token, so redirects are not needed in that stronger scenario. Accidental/misconfigured redirects and HTTP on-path injection are the relevant incremental exposures.
findings.impact: FRM credentials can leave the selected origin. This is source/spec-supported; a Chromium/browser integration proof was not run because the sandbox denied a local listener with EPERM.

evidence.claim: Custom token header with fetch(url,{headers}) and no redirect policy
POST uses the same custom header and default redirect policy
API Explorer duplicates an unguarded authenticated fetch

findings.remediation: Set redirect:'error' on every authenticated FRM request and consolidate API Explorer through the same transport policy. Ask users to configure a canonical final server origin. Do not rely on checking response.redirected or response.url after following because the token may already have been sent. Keep tokens keyed to exact normalized origin.
acceptance_tests: A permitted local mock server returns 301/302/303/307/308 to a second mock origin; the second origin receives zero requests and zero token bytes.
Same-origin redirects are rejected consistently by the chosen simple policy; explain canonical-endpoint remediation in UI.
GET, chat POST and API Explorer all exercise the same redirect and token policy.
Tests use dummy tokens, isolated server ports and explicit CORS fixtures; run once in supported browser and once in the chosen Electron runtime.
findings.diagnostic: audit_work/renderer_diagnostics.json (request options inspected; live redirect test blocked)

findings.title: FRM credentials are persisted in renderer localStorage by default without an explicit secret lifecycle
findings.summary: Every config edit serializes the complete config, including password, to localStorage. It is restored automatically on startup. The password-type input masks display but does not protect storage. Host changes preserve the previous password through object spreading, and no distinct Forget Token/connection-generation boundary exists.
findings.preconditions: A party can read the relevant browser/Electron profile or execute JavaScript in that renderer origin. No independent renderer XSS or unrestricted remote read of localStorage was demonstrated. Endpoint changes create an additional user-error disclosure risk when the old token is retained for a different chosen server.
findings.impact: Long-lived FRM tokens persist in a renderer-readable profile and can be reused after app close or accidentally submitted to another server. This does not establish an unauthenticated remote exploit by itself.

evidence.claim: Full config including password is restored and stored
Host/port edits retain password; token input is only visually masked
Connection result lacks a generation check and config edits merely toggle connected false

findings.remediation: Keep the FRM credential in session memory in both browser and desktop. Persist only schema-validated nonsecret preferences. Protected persistent secret storage is deferred (ADR-003). Delete legacy password fields during idempotent settings migration. Clear the live token on reload, restart, Forget, or any change of canonical origin. Cancel old requests and invalidate their generation before replacing the connection. Do not export tokens or restore them from backups.
acceptance_tests: After saving/reloading settings, active localStorage and new settings/theme exports contain no dummy token.
Legacy password migration preserves valid nonsecret settings; interrupted migration never revives a secret. Historical filesystem backups are outside app erasure control.
Forget, restart, reload, origin change and token change clear/invalidate the applicable live secret, cancel work and initiate owned-tunnel teardown before replacement.
A blocked request to A followed by a change to B cannot mark B connected or send the token for A to B.
No remember-token feature or plaintext fallback is introduced in either platform during this security release; later OS-protected persistence requires a separate decision and tests.

findings.title: Remote responses and polling have no application-level schema, size, deadline, or concurrency bounds
findings.summary: fetchEndpoint<T> returns response.json() without runtime validation or request/body bounds. Several components assume arrays and scalar field types. Polling uses setInterval without abort or single-flight control. The one-hour buffer prunes by time only and retains whole snapshots. API Explorer has a second unbounded JSON path.
findings.preconditions: A configured FRM server, mod incompatibility, corrupted network response, large factory, or malicious API response supplies malformed/large/slow data. Local configuration tampering can also make refresh values invalid; the normal UI restricts selectable rates.
findings.impact: Renderer crashes, excessive CPU/memory, stale data and accumulated requests are possible. No measured production DoS or RCE is claimed; browser networking imposes some independent implementation limits.

evidence.claim: No schema/body/deadline/abort controls; connectivity accepts any OK JSON
Unvalidated response and fixed-interval polling
Array/string/number assumptions in render
Polling can overlap and cleanup only clears the timer
Remote scalar/array assumptions
Whole snapshots retained with a time bound but no count/byte bound
Separate unbounded response parser

findings.remediation: Create a small shared bounded request/polling layer with per-endpoint validators, response-byte caps, a deadline covering body reads, caller cancellation, one in-flight request per endpoint and stale-generation rejection. Validate persisted settings. Keep only bounded/aggregated history. Keep prior valid data visibly stale after rejection; provide recovery without crashing the entire app. Preserve escaped React text rendering.
acceptance_tests: Wrong top-level shape, wrong scalar type, oversized strings and over-limit streamed/chunked bodies produce an explicit recoverable error, not an unhandled render exception.
A never-resolving response is aborted by a controlled deadline; unmount/origin change aborts it earlier.
Barrier-based overlapping tick test never sees more than one in-flight request per origin/endpoint.
Fake clock plus max-sized fixtures prove history count/byte bounds across an hour and after clock jumps.
A stale response from a previous connection is discarded and cannot replace newer data.
Large representative legitimate factory fixtures pass chosen limits; limits and tuning decisions are recorded instead of claiming measured capacity now.

findings.title: Unsupported Electron33 engine ships with 46 matching advisories
findings.impact: Desktop runtime remains affected even though Electron is declared as a devDependency. Native browser/Node engine age also lies beyond npm-only coverage. Network-reachable TLS and conditional contextBridge issues justify prompt upgrade; API-specific advisories are not all proven reachable.
findings.remediation: Proposed target Electron45.2.1, using build Node24.22.1 or newer supported24.x security patch. Rebuild both Windows and Linux; verify embedded versions from artifacts and update Electron hardening. Target is metadata-checked, not build-tested.
acceptance: No Electron33 artifacts distributed after migration
Supported engine and exact Chromium/Node versions recorded in release SBOM
Full lockfile rescan and artifact startup/network/IPC tests pass
Each retained advisory has reviewer, rationale, expiry and revisit trigger

observations.title: No explicit CSP/permission policy; file protocol and development-mode production switch need hardening
observations.detail: No CSP or permission handler was found in the inspected source; the packaged document is file:// and development content can be selected by NODE_ENV or --dev without app.isPackaged gating. These increase the consequence of untrusted content but do not establish XSS on their own. Prefer a fixed app origin, deny unneeded permissions, and a production CSP compatible with Next static export: hash required inline bootstrap scripts, avoid script unsafe-inline/eval, constrain connect-src to selected FRM endpoints, and self-host fonts if feasible. Do not add a blanket policy that breaks required FRM connections or silently weaken it with wildcards.

observations.title: Patch-only security versions deliberately do not produce releases
observations.detail: A patch bump inside the same major.minor is skipped. A source security fix shipped only as 1.5.1 after 1.5.0 will not automatically produce release artifacts through this workflow. Plan a reviewed release policy that can publish every security fix, or explicitly choose a minor version when using the existing policy. This is a deterministic release-policy limitation, not a privilege exploit.

observations.title: Repository does not enforce release signing/provenance evidence
observations.detail: No required signing, signature verification or external native-binary manifest gate is visible in these files. This is not proof that published binaries are unsigned; external build environment/secrets and actual release artifacts were not inspected. Add verifiable hashes/SBOM and platform signing/provenance as appropriate after selecting the delivery process.
